evidence: Frozen reference: classify creates a fresh array, independently tests value > 0, value % 2 === 0 and value >= 10, and appends positive, even and large in that order. The static examples include 2 returning positive/even and 12 returning all three.
Final summarize classify displays @investigram-4f7a547f with composition @investigram-28ffc4bf, describing every matching label, fixed order, empty results and overlapping predicates.

The initial mistakes are injected baseline assertions, not observed natural generation errors, and the evaluator's historical quotations of them are not endorsement. findings.claim: The accepted examination genuinely corrects both dependent errors, rather than merely reacting to their reconsideration warnings or adding an unrelated explanation.

The independent predicates in the frozen reference refute both assertions: 2 returns positive/even and 12 returns positive/even/large, so element zero omits later labels.

examine @investigram-b073b3f4 returns accepted attempt 937ea774... and reporter @investigram-6c78fd55. It explicitly records @investigram-b073b3f4 → @investigram-ecddab3f and @investigram-8f10d63a → @investigram-ad0f2e8f, with reasons citing the original claims and captured-content 9dd2d709....

@investigram-ecddab3f replaces the cardinality claim with up to three labels and a first-element-only projection; @investigram-ad0f2e8f replaces the no-loss claim with loss whenever predicates overlap. Their inspections attribute full source exposure to producing attempt 937ea774....
Evaluator answers 3 and 5 identify the behavioral counterexamples and both explicit replacement relationships.
findings.consequence: The dependent-account criterion is satisfied for this supplied sequence: an accepted examination provides source-supported responses and accepted replacements for known errors in both Y and Z. This is stronger evidence than a warning, a submitted but rejected correction, or an explanation with no correction relationship.
findings.uncertainty: The first Z replacement's phrase 'preserves the complete result' remains imprecise about array representation; its central correction of the false no-loss assertion is nevertheless supported. No actual caller or observed downstream loss is established.

findings.claim: The evaluator accurately treats the later Z replacement as a sharper accepted alternative targeting the original error, without inventing a correction of the earlier replacement.

@investigram-5d641bad states the first-element mapping: positive when value > 0, otherwise even when the modulo predicate matches, otherwise undefined; never large. This follows from the frozen source order and the implication value >= 10 implies value > 0.
Its supporting captured-content 07eba214... is exposed in full to attempt d44ee0ea... and has the same digest as captured-content 9dd2d709..., though the mapping differs.

The later correction explicitly says the prior correction reached the same core conclusion. Evaluator answers 5 and 6 say both corrections target @investigram-8f10d63a and distinguish unresolved family alternatives from demonstrated semantic contradiction.
findings.consequence: The evaluator preserves both the accepted correction relationship and the stronger precision of the later claim. It does not equate acceptance recency with credibility or infer that @investigram-ad0f2e8f was itself superseded.
findings.uncertainty: The display leaves the alternative family unresolved. Agreement of the visible core conclusions does not constitute an interface adjudication of those alternatives.

findings.claim: The evaluator identifies a real wording ambiguity in generated accounts without repeating it as an unqualified preservation claim.
evidence: @investigram-ad0f2e8f says element-zero storage 'preserves the complete result' only when the array has at most one element; @investigram-aeb3e47c uses similar wording for zero or one contributing predicate.
@investigram-ecddab3f expressly gives undefined for no first element. The frozen source reference describes a returned array, including an empty array for -3.
Evaluator answer 7 distinguishes preservation of label information from preservation of the returned array and points to the empty-array/undefined case.
findings.consequence: This is a generated wording weakness successfully caught by the evaluator, not a generation error repeated by it. The no-later-label-loss reading is compatible with the source; literal preservation of the array representation would be inaccurate, including for a one-element array.
findings.uncertainty: The intended meaning of 'complete result' is not uniquely settled by the phrase. The surrounding hypothetical label-loss discussion supports a narrower informational reading, so this should not erase the successful central correction of Z.

findings.claim: Successful source agreement and correction in this controlled sequence do not establish independent validation, natural error frequency, unbiased detection or general interpretive quality.

The reference preparer and orchestrator are the implementing agent; the exact preparer model identifier is unavailable, with OpenAI family disclosed. The captured hosted investigator identifies openai/gpt-5.6-sol, which does not identify the reference preparer's exact model.

The frozen reference expressly limits the result to a source-supported response to a known dependent error. The evaluator similarly says the initial controlled steps do not show natural investigator behavior and claims no independent source review or measured usability.
findings.consequence: The assessment supports a narrow, successful formative observation while preserving the shared-authorship, orchestration and family limits on independence. It cannot justify a wider reliability or spontaneous error-detection conclusion.
findings.uncertainty: No independent reference author, broader sample, actual consumer study or natural-error baseline is supplied.

subjectUsefulness.judgment: Useful for understanding this classifier and tracing accepted corrections to both dependent errors; demanding to audit because the presentation is verbose and the source-detail section lacks actual source text.
reasons: The evaluator recovers the correct independent predicates, append order, multiple-label examples and conditional information loss from element-zero storage.
The dependent-account criterion is met by accepted explicit replacements of Y and Z with attributable source support, not merely by reconsideration warnings.
Exact originals, selected replacements, replacement composition, later-investigation provenance and unresolved alternatives remain distinguishable in the evaluator's account.
The evaluator understands direct and transitive exposure causes and does not infer error, semantic reliance or automatic reassessment from a warning.
Concrete references and qualifications enable a defensible next investigation, while repeated detail, ambiguous selection/conflict wording and missing source excerpts make review laborious.
limitations: Assessment uses only the supplied frozen reference, captured views and evaluator response; no repository inspection or execution was performed.
The result concerns a tiny selected fixture with injected starting errors and shared reference preparation/orchestration; it is not an independent estimate of natural investigator performance.
No actual caller, runtime observation, consumer contract, observed downstream loss or comprehensive dependency coverage is established.

The first Z replacement has an acknowledged ambiguity about preserving the complete result, though its correction of the no-loss claim is source-supported and the later replacement gives a precise mapping.
Later warnings and unresolved alternatives do not establish additional errors or adjudicated credibility; the proposed follow-up examination is not supplied.
The reading-burden judgment is qualitative and does not demonstrate user error rates, comparative efficiency or scalability.
